newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farmers to get 1.2 billion marks for BSE.
newsitem.headline: German farmers to get 1.2 billion marks for BSE.

text.p: The German government said on Monday it would make 1.2 billion marks available to farmers to help to compensate them for losses connected with "mad cow disease" or BSE.

A spokesman said the money would be made available by postponing for two years until January 1999 a plan to scrap tax-free allowances for major farms, worth 600 million marks a year. Half the money will come from Bonn, half from the federal states.

The German farmers' association DBV reacted angrily to the news, saying the maintenance of the tax break would do nothing to ease the situation of farmers who have suffered from a sharp drop in beef sales.

The government spokesman said Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Agriculture Minister Jochen Borchert would seek ways to make up for the shortfall in budget revenue without increasing government borrowing. --Bonn newsroom +49-228 26097160
